description: Start with Run Summary and Subsystem Health for the selected variables and time range, then expand the diagnostic rows. Select one run for diagnosis or multiple run IDs for comparison; cold/warm uses the same view. Colors are attention signals, not universal pass/fail.

options.content:
### Scope: `${run_id:text}` · `${test_name:text}` · `${api_name:text}`
Worst/total for selected runs/time. Table keeps Run ID. Red/orange = investigate; blue/purple = neutral, not a verdict.

panels.description: Worst p95 and p99 per selected run in the current time range. These values are informational because each k6 run can use different thresholds.
panels.title: k6 Latency

panels.description: Worst failure rate and check success per selected run. Orange means at least one failure or an incomplete check; compare with the threshold recorded in the JSON report.
panels.title: k6 Reliability

panels.description: Completed and dropped iterations per selected run. Dropped iterations above zero indicate that the configured arrival rate was not fully delivered.
panels.title: k6 Load Delivery

panels.description: Worst server-side p95 and p99 across Spring routes in the selected time range. Use the detailed HTTP row to identify the route and status.
panels.title: Spring HTTP

panels.description: Peak application CPU, heap usage, and Tomcat busy-thread ratio in the selected time range. Treat these as workload context, not universal pass/fail limits.
panels.title: App Saturation

panels.description: Peak pending connections and connection timeouts in the selected range. Any non-zero value is a direct signal to inspect the Hikari detail row.
panels.title: Hikari Pool

panels.description: Hit ratio and Redis error signals for the selected range. No cache traffic remains No data; it is not converted into a zero-percent hit ratio.
panels.title: Redis Health

panels.description: Peak connections, long-running transactions, deadlocks, and slowest statement mean time for the selected database and time range.

targets.expr: topk(1, 1000 * sum by (datname, queryid) (increase(pg_stat_statements_seconds_total{application="nook-postgres",datname=~"${database:regex}"}[$__range])) / clamp_min(sum by (datname, queryid) (increase(pg_stat_statements_calls_total{application="nook-postgres",datname=~"${database:regex}"}[$__range])), 1))

panels.title: Postgres

panels.description: Selected request names ranked by their worst p95 in the current time range. The table includes setup or smoke request names when API Name is All; narrow the variable to focus on a target API.
panels.title: Top API Offenders by p95
k6 API Latency by Name
panels.description: Client-observed k6 p95 and p99 per request name. Cold and warm requests remain separate through their request names and run IDs.

panels.title: k6 Failure Rate and Checks
panels.description: k6 failure rate and checks per selected run. Consult the JSON report for the exact threshold used by that run.

panels.title: k6 Iterations and Dropped Iterations
panels.description: Completed and dropped iterations per run and scenario. Dropped iterations mean the configured arrival rate was not fully delivered.

panels.title: Spring HTTP Request Rate
panels.description: Spring request throughput by method, route, and status. Compare a rate change with the selected k6 run and latency panels.

panels.title: Spring HTTP Latency
panels.description: Spring p95 and p99 by method and route. Use this to distinguish client-observed k6 latency from server-side request handling.

panels.title: JVM Process CPU
panels.description: Application and system CPU utilization over time. Correlate sustained peaks with latency and dropped iterations.

panels.title: JVM Memory
panels.description: JVM heap and non-heap used versus max memory. Inspect growth and recovery around the selected run.

targets.expr: sum by (action, cause) (rate(jvm_gc_pause_seconds_sum{application="$application"}[1m])) / sum by (action, cause) (rate(jvm_gc_pause_seconds_count{application="$application"}[1m]))

panels.title: JVM GC Pause
panels.description: Mean JVM GC pause and pause-event rate. Correlate pause bursts with application latency and memory pressure.

panels.title: Tomcat Threads
panels.description: Tomcat busy, current, and configured maximum threads. Sustained busy/max convergence indicates servlet-thread saturation.

panels.title: Hikari Connections
panels.description: Hikari active, pending, and idle connections. Pending growth suggests the database pool is becoming a bottleneck.

panels.title: Hikari Connection Timeouts
panels.description: Hikari timeout counter and five-minute increase. Any increase during a run requires connection-pool investigation.

panels.title: Redis Keyspace Hits, Misses, and Ratio
panels.description: Redis hits, misses, and hit ratio. Cold runs should show misses; warm runs should show increased hits without mixing run IDs.

panels.title: Redis Command Mean Latency
panels.description: Mean Redis command latency by command. Inspect the highest commands when cache operations coincide with API latency.

panels.title: Redis Commands and Connections
panels.description: Redis command throughput and connected clients. Use this as workload context rather than a universal health threshold.

panels.title: Redis Errors
panels.description: Redis command failures, rejected connections, and exporter availability. Non-zero values are direct investigation signals.

panels.title: PostgreSQL Connections
panels.description: PostgreSQL backends, configured connection limit, and long-running transactions for the selected database.

panels.title: PostgreSQL Locks and Transactions
panels.description: PostgreSQL locks, commit/rollback rate, and deadlocks. Deadlocks are direct investigation signals; locks require workload context.

panels.title: PostgreSQL Statement Mean Time
panels.description: Top statement query IDs by mean execution time from pg_stat_statements. SQL text is intentionally not exposed.

title: NOOK API Observability
